findings.claim: The passage self-contradicts inside paragraph 5: it first names four distinct causes of a no-detection result, one of which is the forecast being wrong, and then treats the no-detection results of the control flights as if they established that the forecast was wrong - and calls that finding a product of paperwork rather than of the imagery it has just discredited.
findings.evidence: Paragraph 4: "Of 141 flights that were left alone and flew straight through a forecast layer, 61 left a mark anybody could find afterward. The forecast was calling for wet air a good deal more often than the sky supplied it." Paragraph 5: "And a success looks like an empty picture. So does a forecast that was wrong, and a contrail too thin to register, and a sheet of cloud sitting over the top of one." Also paragraph 5: "The picture is flat, so nothing in it says how high the thing is. On a busy evening four or five tracks cross the same square of sky." And the closing: "the findings that will outlast the trial are his: that the forecast asks for more descents than the sky calls for, and that most of the descents it asks for are never flown. Both of those come off records the center already keeps."
findings.why: The 80 control flights that left no mark are, by the writer's own enumeration six sentences later, ambiguous between four causes (forecast wrong / contrail too thin to register / overlying cloud sheet / misattribution among four or five tracks). The over-calling finding is therefore exactly as dependent on the imagery as the satellite count the writer dismisses as "the smallest thing those two winters produced", and "Both of those come off records the center already keeps" is false of the first finding - only the 96-of-406 take-rate finding comes off center paperwork. This is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: Q4's key C ("Many of the descents that were flown will have bought nothing") is inferred from the over-calling finding, and Q5's key A ("He thinks it settled less than the center's own records did") is the writer's ranking of the two. Neither key flips, because the passage asserts "The forecast was calling for wet air a good deal more often than the sky supplied it" in the writer's own voice and ELF convention takes the page as authority - hence NOTES, not REFUTED. But a self-contradiction that undercuts the premise of one key and the coherence of another is precisely what the integrated stage exists to catch, and it survived into candidates-final unrepaired.

findings.claim: Q1's WHY-DISTRACTORS makes two false statements about the passage in order to dismiss option C.
findings.evidence: Q1 rationale: "C = surface_word_match - it recycles the passage's most distinctive vocabulary (crystals, ice, wet air) into a topic that is disposed of in a single clause of paragraph 1; the growth mechanism matters here only because it explains why the layer is invisible." Paragraph 1 in fact devotes its last four sentences to it: "Usually that air is dry with respect to ice, the crystals hand their water back, and the line behind the wing is gone inside a minute or two. Sometimes it is not dry. In a layer already carrying more vapor than ice can hold at that temperature, the crystals do not shrink but feed, and go on feeding, so that by the time a contrail is an hour old most of the ice in it was never inside an engine. It came out of the air the airplane was passing through." Invisibility is explained in paragraph 2 by a different mechanism: "starting a crystal from nothing needs roughly half again as much vapor as keeping an existing one alive."
findings.why: The rationale is the teaching payload a student reads after answering. "Disposed of in a single clause" is checkable in five seconds and is wrong - option C's content is the closing half of paragraph 1 and the paragraph's punchline ("most of the ice in it was never inside an engine"). "Matters here only because it explains why the layer is invisible" is also wrong: crystal growth explains contrail persistence and the ambient-ice origin; the nucleation-threshold gap in paragraph 2 is what explains invisibility. The key (B) is unaffected - C is still a part-for-whole answer to a main-idea stem - so this is a rationale-accuracy defect, not a key defect. The same false characterisation is repeated in generator_meta.self_blind_solve ("Q1/C by the single clause the growth mechanism actually gets"), so it was carried forward rather than caught.

findings.claim: Q3's WHY-DISTRACTORS defeats option C with a claim the passage does not make, importing outside knowledge to settle a within-passage question.
findings.evidence: Q3 rationale: "C = quantifier_upgrade turned into a reversal - the passage says the daylight effects pull against one another, which is a partial cancellation, not a change of sign". The passage says only: "in daylight a spreading contrail also turns some sunlight back toward space, and the two effects pull against one another, while after dark there is nothing pulling the other way." It never says which side wins, never uses the words warm, cool or climate (0 occurrences of each in the passage), and never quantifies the offset. generator_meta.mechanism_verification_note (8) sources the partial-cancellation sign externally (Stuber and Forster 2007; Teoh et al. 2024, which it concedes finds 03:00-12:00 LT contrails "most likely to end up net cooling").
findings.why: "Pull against one another" is silent on net sign; the correct refutation of C is that the passage simply does not state it, not that the passage states partial cancellation. Teaching a student that the text asserted a sign it did not assert is the same move the unit's other rationales correctly condemn as outside_knowledge. C is still not defensible as the answer (D is stated almost verbatim), so no key change.

findings.claim: Q3's key D introduces a proposition the passage never states, and the rationale's claim that D "adds nothing" is inaccurate; the item is also labelled direct detail retrieval while requiring an inference step.
findings.evidence: Key D: "After dark nothing works against the warming, since no sunlight is turned away." Q3 rationale: "D restates that in different words and adds nothing." The words warm/warming, cool/cooling and climate appear 0 times in the passage; "effect" appears exactly once, in "the two effects pull against one another", and the first of those two effects is never introduced anywhere in the text. generator_meta.question_families labels Q3 "ELF-TYPE-001" (direct detail retrieval).
findings.why: The definite "the two effects" has no antecedent for its first member, so D's "the warming" is supplied by the student, not by the page. It is a one-step entailment (if one effect sends sunlight back to space and the two oppose each other, the other must warm), so D survives as the single best option and the key stands - a complaining student is answerable. But "adds nothing" is false, and a retrieval-labelled item that requires the reader to name an effect the passage withholds sits awkwardly against the zero-prior-knowledge pillar. The cleanest repair is one clause in paragraph 3 naming the warming side, or a key phrased as "nothing pulls the other way after dark, because no sunlight is turned back".
